reason: Cross-striolate (moss peristome teeth, seed ribs) = finely marked with lines running across the long axis, which is PATO:0002478 transversely striated; the diminutive 'striolate' only says the lines are fine.

A comparison that needs its second term: increased length (PATO_0000573) towards the other part (slot 3). 'longer than or equalling X' is a union with the equality pattern (docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md).

Not a quality: the stalk of the named organ (pinna, fruit, frond, seed cone), measured for length (PATO_0000122) as a part of the bearer (slot 1). A fruit stalk could be read more exactly as a pedicel.

Covered with small bristles tipped with glands; FLOPO:0991173 is defined as at least some hairs being gland-tipped, which covers bristly gland-tipped hairs. Not stipitate-glandular, which means stalked glands.
A fruit opening into two valves: a count of 2 fruit valves (PO_0000033) set in the word, like '3-valved'. Dehiscence (FLOPO:0991149) is implied.
French 'inerme' = unarmed: without spines, thorns or prickles. PATO:0001365 spiny covers spines, thorns and similar projections, so the negation fits better than three separate absence statements.

label: catkin-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's architecture resembling a catkin, a dense, often pendulous spike of small, reduced, usually unisexual flowers. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991142 spike-like and PATO:0002455 corymb-like, worded as they are; the inflorescence itself is PO:0030119 catkin inflorescence.
reason: Used for inflorescences and gymnosperm pollen cones that look like catkins without being catkins; it fits beside the raceme-like and spike-like classes added in the last review.
FLOPO:0991020 foetid is defined as an unpleasant, offensive odour and already has the synonym 'unpleasant smell'.
A faint purple colour over the part: the colour is purple; 'tinged' only says it is weak or partial and is lost, as with other degree words.
'Several' is not a number, so the count pattern cannot hold it; the firm content is that veins are present (as rule C211 'veined').
A paleate receptacle (Asteraceae) bears chaff scales, which PO has as flower bract (synonym chaff). For grass florets 'with a palea', the part is palea (PO_0009038) present.
A shape between two existing values: triangular (PATO_0001875, synonym deltoid) and ovate (FLOPO:0991024); a compound, not a new term.

label: berry-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a fruit by virtue of its being fleshy and juicy throughout, like a berry, whatever its actual fruit type. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991042 cherry-like; the fruit type itself is PO:0030108 berry fruit.
reason: Floras use it for fruits that are not berries (pomes, drupes, capsules, mericarps) but look like them, so the PO fruit type cannot be used.
A compound of raceme-like (FLOPO:0991197) and panicle-like (FLOPO:0991198): a panicle whose branches are raceme-like, or a form between the two.

label: scape-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a stem by virtue of its being an erect flowering axis that is leafless or nearly so and rises from a basal tuft of leaves, like a scape. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002457 leaf-like; the scape itself is mapped to PO:0009053 peduncle (rule C255).
reason: Describes flowering stems that are true stems but look like scapes; mapping them to peduncle would be wrong.
Lateral veins joined into loops near the margin. In the vein itself this is FLOPO:0991128 anastomosing (branches rejoining); in the leaf the same arrangement is PATO_0001970 brochidodromous.

label: hemiepiphytic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its spending only part of its life as an epiphyte, either starting on a host and later rooting in the ground or starting in the ground and later losing its connection to it. NOTE: Probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives); sibling of FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic, not a child, because the plant is not always epiphytic.
reason: A recognised habit of aroids, figs and Clusia, different from epiphytic, terrestrial and climbing; follows the precedent of FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic.

label: samara-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being a dry, flat body extended into one or more membranous wings, like a samara. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991042 cherry-like; the fruit type itself is PO:0030099 samara fruit.
reason: Used for pods, mericarps and seeds that look like samaras without being samara fruits, so the PO fruit type cannot be used.
French 'déhiscence loculicide' = loculicidal, added in the last review as FLOPO:0991152.
A moss leaf-cell shape between oblong (PATO_0000946) and rhomboid (PATO_0001938); a compound of two existing values.
Acuminate (PATO_0002228) tending towards caudate (PATO_0001880), with 'sub-' marking the approximate value; a compound of two existing values (pattern 01 plus the continuum), not a new term.

The source words are French 'trinervé(e)s' = 3-veined: a count of 3 veins (PO_0005020) in the word. 'Triviate' is a faulty normalised form; where the veins arise above the base, the reading is FLOPO:0991202 triplinerved.
There is no positive term to negate: 'proliferous' (bearing plantlets or buds, or viviparous spikelets) has no term, and PATO_0002102 proliferative is a cell quality. Review 'proliferous' first.

target: new: compound of two values that hold together (intersection)
reason: Serrate (PATO_0001206) with teeth ending in small spines (FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped on the teeth, slot 1); both values hold at once, so it is a combination, not a new term.
A scant pappus or indumentum has few, scattered bristles or hairs: PATO:0001609 sparse.
Stipellate = bearing stipels at the base of the leaflets, like stipulate (C210); 'folioles sans stipelles' is the absence.

label: strobilate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's architecture resembling a strobilus: a compact axis covered by closely overlapping bracts or scales. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991142 spike-like; not PATO:0002021 conical, which is the geometric cone shape; the structure itself is PO:0025083 strobilus.
reason: Used for spikes and racemes with closely overlapping bracts (Acanthaceae, Zingiberaceae) that look like cones; there is no PATO term and the PO strobilus does not fit angiosperm inflorescences.
Pressed against the axis while pointing upwards; the defining content is FLOPO:0991064 appressed, and erect (PATO_0000622) adds nothing beyond the direction along the axis.

target: berry-like (new class proposed for 'berrylike' in this batch)
reason: Bacciform = berry-like; a synonym of the class proposed for 'berrylike' above, not a second class.
A specialist type name for the fern endodermis that only makes sense with its typology. A term would be doubtful without a sourced definition, and it is too rare.
